clue.text: Substantial food male chewed after nine?

indicators.note: after places the chewed letters behind the number word in the answer

parts.note: nine is three times three, a square number

indicators.note: something chewed is mangled, so the letters of male are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A man munching his food after the ninth hour, or perhaps after nine holes of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags nine as an example: it is three times three. 'chewed' is the anagram signal and 'after' orders the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: A proper, filling meal is idiomatically called a square one.

clue.text: Broadcast offered to viewers, hard to miss

indicators.note: to miss here means the letter for hard goes absent from the word

parts.note: a programme offered to viewers has been shown
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A programme offered to viewers that was hard to miss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to miss' drops the H from SHOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Seed that is broadcast is scattered by hand over a field, i.e. sown.

clue.text: Exercised and entertained, but not in the morning

indicators.note: not says the morning letters are left out of the word for entertained

parts.note: entertained means amused
AM, ante meridiem, marks times in the morning

explanation.surface: Someone who got exercise and fun, but only later in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: A right or power that is exercised has been employed or put to use.

clue.text: Artist starts to receive eulogies — number one, right?

indicators.note: starts to picks the opening letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An artist begins to receive praise and asks if he is now top of the pile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes R and E from 'receive eulogies'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir was a French Impressionist painter.

clue.text: Solution to a problem with troublesome little characters?

definitions.text: Solution to a problem with troublesome little characters?

parts.words: Solution to a problem with troublesome little characters?
parts.note: the troublesome little characters are tiny printed letters that are hard to read, and the fix is a lens that enlarges them

explanation.surface: A remedy for dealing with mischievous children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little characters' suggests naughty youngsters but means small print.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand lens enlarges small print, solving the difficulty of reading it.

clue.text: Two articles on musician's original piece for church choir

parts.note: AN is the indefinite article
THE is the definite article

indicators.note: original picks the first letter of the word for the performer

explanation.surface: A musician's composition for a church choir, with a couple of articles written about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A short choral composition sung in church services is the classic sense of this word.

clue.text: Medicine from doctor that gets you recovering finally

parts.note: U is text-speak for you

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word for getting better

explanation.surface: A doctor's medicine that finally gets you on the road to recovery.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmaceutical remedy is a medicine.

clue.text: Second match is rarer game, I fancy

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means imagine, but as an adjective it hints at elaborate rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a second wedding is like rarer quarry for a hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I fancy' looks like an opinion; 'fancy' is the anagram indicator and 'I' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A match is a marriage, so a second one is a later wedding.

clue.text: Items of food supplied by sporting venue not at all sensible

parts.note: a football ground is a sporting venue
nuts means crazy

explanation.surface: Snacks sold at a stadium are senseless.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanuts are also called by this name and are eaten as food.

clue.text: Little sirs appearing evenings Monday to Friday

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little
knights are addressed as Sir

explanation.surface: Small gentlemen turn up on working-day evenings.
explanation.definitionFit: The working days' nights are the evenings of Monday to Friday.

clue.text: Military supplies carried by team mostly

indicators.note: carried by means the letters are held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A team bearing most of the army's provisions.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammunition, shortened, is the munitions supplied to troops.

clue.text: Technically sound — if not, price must be adjusted

indicators.note: adjusted signals that the letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A trader insists that if the item is not technically sound, its price must change.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled, competent person is technically sound at what they do.

clue.text: Misconstrue me a lunatic — smear!

indicators.note: misconstrue means interpret wrongly, so the letters are taken in a wrong order

explanation.surface: An indignant protest: misunderstand me as mad and you slander me!
explanation.definitionFit: To slander or defame someone is to smear their name.

clue.text: Doomed rich man embraces trendy theologians

indicators.note: embraces means the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: Dives is the rich man in the parable of Lazarus, condemned to torment
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A wealthy man facing ruin who holds fashionable theologians close.
explanation.definitionFit: Divines is an old word for clergy and religious scholars.

clue.text: I toddle — dislocated muscle

indicators.note: dislocated means put out of place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A toddler wobbles and pulls a shoulder muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: The shoulder's triangular muscle bears this name.

clue.text: Like a fox, inwardly isn't very good

indicators.note: inwardly means the second word sits within the first

parts.note: foxes are proverbially sly
ain't is a colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: Someone cunning like a fox is not really very good inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of saint-like virtue is very good.

clue.text: Lecturer providing book of exercises

definitions.meaning: a senior university lecturer in Britain
a school book of reading passages and exercises

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from reading: a lecturing rank and a school text.

clue.text: Dull little boy's nurse

parts.note: mat or matt means without shine, dull
Ron is a short boy's name

explanation.surface: A boring little lad's nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior nurse in charge of a hospital or school is the matron.

clue.text: Time of nourishment I'd arranged

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has organised the time for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time of nourishment' looks like a mealtime; the definition is just 'Time'.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics, time is treated as the fourth coordinate after the three spatial ones.

clue.text: Frank performed after John

indicators.note: after puts the word for performed behind the toilet word

parts.note: john is slang for a toilet, as is can
performed means did

explanation.surface: Frank went on stage after John.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank and candid both mean open and honest.

clue.text: Antipathy that destroys wonder

indicators.note: destroys says the letters of the following word are broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: A feeling of dislike that kills off any sense of wonder.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a downer on someone is British slang for disliking them.

clue.text: Trifling trickery from what we hear

indicators.note: from what we hear signals that the word for trickery is spoken

parts.note: sleight, as in sleight of hand, is trickery

explanation.surface: Petty deception, according to rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something slight is minor or insignificant, i.e. trifling.

clue.text: Devon town has barn set aside for basic food

indicators.note: set aside means that word is removed from the town name

parts.note: Barnstaple is a market town in Devon, south-west England
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Devon town puts aside a barn for storing basic foodstuffs.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple is a main or essential item of diet.

clue.text: Fearless Tory without gold going after money

indicators.note: going after places the trimmed party word behind the slang for money

parts.note: dough is slang for money

indicators.note: without says those letters are dropped from the party word

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A bold Conservative who has lost his gold chases cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Doughty means brave and resolute, hence fearless.

clue.text: Facing notice say a mild oath

indicators.note: facing means the example abbreviation stands before the notice word

parts.note: EG, for example, is a way of saying say
an ad is a notice

explanation.surface: Confronted with a notice, you might utter a gentle expletive.
explanation.definitionFit: Egad is an old-fashioned exclamation, a softened oath.

clue.text: Body that gets leader deposed roughly

indicators.note: leader deposed means the first letter is taken off

parts.note: the torso is the body's trunk

explanation.surface: A governing body loses its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Or so is an idiom tagged after a figure, meaning approximately.

clue.text: Teams heading off for a day in Rome

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is cut away

parts.note: sides are teams

explanation.surface: Teams depart to spend a day in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ides was a fixed day in the Roman calendar, famously in March.

clue.text: Lacking a burden, travelling light for picnic?

definitions.meaning: playfully, having no picnic basket with you

explanation.definitionFit: Unencumbered means free; the jokey reading is without a picnic basket.

clue.text: Big plant in thoroughfare pruned at edges

indicators.note: pruned at edges says the outer letters are cut

parts.note: a street is a thoroughfare

explanation.surface: A large plant in the road has been trimmed around its edges.
explanation.definitionFit: An oak or ash is a large woody plant.

clue.text: Affluent Italian duke meets American

parts.note: Prospero is the deposed Duke of Milan in Shakespeare's The Tempest

explanation.surface: A wealthy Italian nobleman meets an American.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealthy and affluent are synonyms for well-off.
